skill.name: dotnet-architect
skill.description: Architectural guidance for C# and ASP.NET Core backend systems, covering APIs, data access, caching, testing, and performance.
skill.summary: Design and review production .NET backend architecture with practical C#, ASP.NET Core, EF Core, Dapper, and performance guidance.

content.value_statement: Engineering teams need consistent guidance for building reliable .NET services. This skill guides architecture, implementation, review, and optimization for C# and ASP.NET Core backends.
actual_capabilities: Guides ASP.NET Core API design, middleware choices, dependency injection, and configuration patterns.
Reviews async, LINQ, caching, and data access patterns for performance and maintainability.
Explains EF Core, Dapper, repository, unit of work, and CQRS tradeoffs.
Suggests testing approaches using xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions, WebApplicationFactory, and test containers.
Frames deployment considerations for Docker, Kubernetes, observability, health checks, and CI/CD.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not automated migration or direct code execution.
It depends on user-provided project context, constraints, and existing architecture details.
It does not replace security review, load testing, or production incident response.
It may need current framework documentation for newly released .NET features.

use_cases.title: Plan a New API
use_cases.description: Select architecture patterns, dependency boundaries, and data access strategies for a new ASP.NET Core service.

use_cases.title: Review Backend Code
use_cases.description: Find async, LINQ, caching, and data access issues before they reach production.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Deployment
use_cases.description: Define health checks, logging, OpenTelemetry, Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD practices for .NET services.

prompt_templates.title: Review a .NET API
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my ASP.NET Core API design for maintainability, dependency injection, error handling, and testing. Ask for missing context first.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Data Access Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare EF Core, Dapper, repository, unit of work, and CQRS for this service. Recommend an approach with tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Slow Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this slow .NET endpoint and propose profiling, database, caching, and async improvements. Separate quick wins from larger changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Enterprise Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production ASP.NET Core service for these requirements, including boundaries, data access, caching, observability, testing, and deployment risks.

output_examples.input: Review an order management API for maintainability and production readiness.
output: A prioritized architecture review covering boundaries, dependency injection, validation, error handling, and test gaps.
Recommended improvements separated into immediate fixes, design changes, and operational readiness work.

output_examples.input: Design caching for a product catalog with frequent reads and scheduled imports.
output: A caching strategy using memory and distributed cache layers with explicit invalidation rules.
A risk list covering stale data, concurrency, cache stampedes, and monitoring requirements.

output_examples.input: Optimize a slow search endpoint backed by EF Core.
output_examples.output: A performance plan covering measurement, query shape, indexing, tracking behavior, projection size, pagination, and regression tests.

best_practices: Provide project goals, traffic expectations, data model constraints, and deployment environment before asking for architecture recommendations.
Ask for tradeoffs when choosing between EF Core, Dapper, CQRS, caching, or messaging patterns.
Request test and observability guidance with each design so implementation risks are visible.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a full enterprise architecture without business constraints or operational requirements.
Do not treat generated examples as production code without security review and testing.
Do not optimize every path before identifying measured bottlenecks and user impact.

faq.question: Can this skill write C# code?
faq.answer: It can draft or review C# examples when asked, but it is mainly focused on architecture guidance.

faq.question: Does it support ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Minimal APIs, controllers, middleware, dependency injection, configuration, and request processing.

faq.question: Can it choose between EF Core and Dapper?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains tradeoffs based on query complexity, performance needs, team skills, and maintainability.

faq.question: Is it useful for production readiness reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check health checks, logging, metrics, caching, rate limiting, security, testing, and deployment concerns.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it execute commands or access services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prompt-only guidance and does not include scripts or executable tooling.
